grid_declaration.note: Sanity read, not a validation -- n is small, zero multiple-testing correction across the 6 cells.

signal_extraction.core_decisions_note: core-decisions.jsonl scanned but contributes 0 rows -- its `action` vocabulary is PLACED/HOLD/SKIP_*/RISK_DENY_*/NOT_FLAT, never literally ENTER_BULL/ENTER_BEAR (verified: Counter over all 7924 lines has zero ENTER_BULL/ENTER_BEAR keys).
signal_extraction.independence_caveat: 38 deduped signals span only 10 unique trading days (13 unique day+direction pairs) -- same-day/same-direction clusters (the fleet's 'every strategy runs on every arm' design firing repeatedly as price grinds through one level) are NOT independent draws of the underlying edge; treat n as an upper bound on effective sample size.

data_fetch.granularity_assignment_rule: DATA-DRIVEN: prefer 1m whenever the ACTUAL fetched 1m window covers the signal's entry point with >=14 bars of ATR warmup; else fall back to 1h. NOT a hardcoded 7-day cutoff -- Yahoo's rolling 1m window varies run to run.

cost_model.note: Task-declared friction for this sanity grid ($2.50/side = ~$5/contract round-turn) -- MORE conservative than futures_mirror_shadow.py's own live convention (~$1.24/contract round-turn, closing fills only).

entry_convention: Entry fills at the OPEN of the first bar STRICTLY AFTER the signal timestamp (skips the signal's own bar), matching backtest/futures/swing_sim.py's documented next-bar-open-after-signal convention.
fill_conventions: Stop legs (fixed pre-TP1 AND the post-TP1 trailing stop) use futures.fill_sim_broker.gap_aware_stop_fill (imported) -- in-bar touch fills AT the stop, a bar whose OPEN already gapped through fills AT THE OPEN (worse). TP1 and time-flat/deadline fills use touch-at-level / bar-open, no slippage -- identical to futures_mirror_shadow.py's own documented FILL CONVENTIONS.
known_limitations: 1h-granularity trades are LOW-FIDELITY for stop/TP touch order (an hourly bar's high/low can straddle both a stop and a target; stop-first convention applied).
15:55 ET deadline checked at each bar's OPEN, not continuously -- can overrun the true deadline by up to one bar-width (~55min on 1h, <1min on 1m).

ATR14 computed on the SAME granularity as that trade's fills (task-directed), NOT the live spec's true 5-minute ES window -- 1h-trade R-distances differ from what the live mirror would actually compute for the same moment.
Same-day/same-direction signal clusters inflate n without adding independent evidence -- see signal_extraction.independence_caveat.

1h.interpretation: ratio >~0.5 means a SINGLE bar's typical range can cover half the stop distance on its own -- stop risks sitting inside routine bar noise on this granularity. ratio <~0.3 means the stop is comfortably wider than typical single-bar chop.

1m.interpretation: ratio >~0.5 means a SINGLE bar's typical range can cover half the stop distance on its own -- stop risks sitting inside routine bar noise on this granularity. ratio <~0.3 means the stop is comfortably wider than typical single-bar chop.

null_buy_and_hold.description: Same signal timestamps/directions, ENTRY_QTY (2 contracts) held flat to the same 2-session 15:55 ET deadline, NO stop/target. 'Does the mirror spec beat just holding the direction.'
